indicators.name: Prevalence of undernourishment
indicators.definition: Share of the population whose habitual food consumption is insufficient to provide the dietary energy needed for a normal, active, healthy life.
indicators.notes: Three-year moving averages; not directly comparable with survey-based food insecurity measures.

indicators.name: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in the population
indicators.definition: Share of the population experiencing severe food insecurity, measured with the Food Insecurity Experience Scale.
indicators.targetNote: Target 2.1: ensure access to food for all by 2030
indicators.notes: Severe level only; the moderate-or-severe series is a separate variable.

indicators.name: Proportion of children moderately or severely stunted, under 5 years old
indicators.definition: Share of children under 5 whose height for age is more than two standard deviations below the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
indicators.targetNote: Target 2.2: end all forms of malnutrition by 2030
indicators.notes: Joint Child Malnutrition Estimates combine many surveys, so year-to-year change is smoothed.

indicators.name: Proportion of children moderately or severely wasted, under 5 years old
indicators.definition: Share of children under 5 whose weight for height is more than two standard deviations below the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
indicators.targetNote: Target 2.2: end all forms of malnutrition by 2030
indicators.notes: Survey-driven, so many countries have only a few observations.

indicators.name: Proportion of population below the international poverty line
indicators.definition: Share of the population living below the international poverty line, expressed in purchasing-power-adjusted dollars per person per day.
indicators.targetNote: Target 1.1: eradicate extreme poverty for all people by 2030
indicators.notes: Household surveys are irregular, and the poverty line is revised when purchasing-power data are updated.

indicators.name: Employed population below the international poverty line, 15 years and over
indicators.definition: Share of employed people aged 15 and over who live in households below the international poverty line.
indicators.targetNote: Target 1.1: eradicate extreme poverty for all people by 2030
indicators.notes: Covers a smaller set of countries than the headline poverty series.

indicators.name: Proportion of youth not in education, employment or training, 15 to 24 years old
indicators.short: Youth not in work or school
indicators.definition: Share of young people aged 15 to 24 who are neither employed nor in education or training. This series follows the previous ILO definition.
indicators.targetNote: Target 8.6: substantially reduce this share by 2020
indicators.notes: Previous ILO definition; the current-definition series is reported separately by ILO.

indicators.name: Unemployment rate, 15 to 24 years old
indicators.definition: Share of the labour force aged 15 to 24 that is without work but available for and seeking employment.
indicators.notes: ILOSTAT series. Two sources report this variable, so values can differ from the primary series.

indicators.name: Proportion of population covered by at least one social protection benefit
indicators.definition: Share of the population receiving at least one social protection cash benefit.
indicators.targetNote: Target 1.3: substantial coverage of the poor and vulnerable by 2030
indicators.notes: Series is short (2015 onward), so long-run trends are not available.

indicators.name: Under-five mortality rate
indicators.definition: Probability of dying between birth and exactly five years of age, expressed per 1,000 live births.
indicators.custodian: UN IGME (UNICEF, WHO, World Bank, UN DESA)
indicators.targetNote: Target 3.2: at least as low as 25 per 1,000 live births by 2030
indicators.notes: Modelled series that pools survey and vital registration data.

indicators.name: Maternal mortality ratio
indicators.definition: Number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.
indicators.custodian: WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank, UN DESA
indicators.targetNote: Target 3.1: fewer than 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030
indicators.disaggregation: Sex = female, as defined in the graph variable
indicators.notes: Estimates carry wide uncertainty intervals that this view does not show.

indicators.name: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.definition: Number of years a newborn would live if prevailing age-specific mortality rates stayed the same throughout life.
indicators.notes: Not an SDG indicator. UNDP HDRO compiles it from UN DESA population estimates.

indicators.name: Universal health coverage service coverage index (2025 methodology)
indicators.definition: Index from 0 to 100 summarising coverage of essential health services across reproductive, child, infectious disease, noncommunicable disease and service-capacity areas.
indicators.targetNote: Target 3.8: achieve universal health coverage by 2030
indicators.notes: Composite index built from tracer indicators; an earlier methodology gives different values.

indicators.name: Proportion of births attended by skilled health personnel
indicators.definition: Share of live births attended by a doctor, nurse or midwife trained to manage normal deliveries and complications.
indicators.notes: High-income countries often report near-universal coverage without recent surveys.

indicators.name: School completion rate, primary education
indicators.definition: Share of children about three to five years older than the intended age for the last grade of primary school who have completed that grade.
indicators.targetNote: Target 4.1: all children complete primary and secondary school by 2030
indicators.notes: Household-survey based; many countries report only every few years.

indicators.name: School completion rate, lower secondary education
indicators.definition: Share of young people about three to five years older than the intended age for the last grade of lower secondary school who have completed that grade.
indicators.targetNote: Target 4.1: all children complete primary and secondary school by 2030
indicators.notes: Household-survey based; many countries report only every few years.

indicators.name: School completion rate, upper secondary education
indicators.definition: Share of young people about three to five years older than the intended age for the last grade of upper secondary school who have completed that grade.
indicators.targetNote: Target 4.1: all children complete primary and secondary school by 2030
indicators.notes: Household-survey based; many countries report only every few years.

indicators.name: Participation rate in organized learning (one year before the official primary entry age)
indicators.definition: Share of children in the year before the official primary entry age who take part in organized learning, including pre-primary or primary education.
indicators.targetNote: Target 4.2: access to early childhood development and pre-primary education by 2030
indicators.notes: Administrative enrolment data combined with population estimates.
